notes:
Identity verified from the supplied source title, Stefanie A. Haller / Eoin T. Flaherty / Ragnhild Balsvik authorship, DOI 10.18718/81781.29, JCRE Volume 2 (2023-3), and complete primary article text through printed p. 30. This is the named replication report, not the original Poole primary paper. No PDF path was supplied; no rendering or acquisition performed.

All assigned descriptions and study identifiers are blank; the sole replication locator is p. 24; Table A2. In this supplied version Table A2 is on printed p. 23 (the source has a preceding repository cover); printed p. 24 contains Table A3. The explicit Table A2 label is used to identify the candidate table. It has four specifications and three replication country/period panels; neither panel, specification, nor coefficient/test is identified by the input. No target is assigned using audit_id, input order, number of assignments, or numeric matching.

Table A2 candidates, columns (1)-(4): Ireland 2005-2010: gamma_M - gamma_D = [0.947, 0.973, 0.129, 0.127], SE = [0.088, 0.088, 0.055, 0.059], printed p = [0.000, 0.000, 0.018, 0.032], N = 1,212,558 in each model. Ireland 2011-2016: gamma_M - gamma_D = [1.110, 1.088, 0.137, 0.137], SE = [0.126, 0.128, 0.018, 0.020], printed p = [0.000, 0.000, 0.000, 0.000], N = 1,396,050 in each model. Norway: gamma_M - gamma_D = [0.611, 0.439, 0.046, 0.047], SE = [0.023, 0.020, 0.010, 0.011], printed p = [0.000, 0.000, 0.000, 0.000], N = 1,697,752 in each model. These are unassigned printed candidates, not selected extracted values. Individual gamma_M and gamma_D coefficients are also printed. F-statistics appear only in the Brazil panel, which reproduces original-study results and cannot supply replication test statistics. No effect-size conversion, test-statistic calculation, p-bound reinterpretation, N sum or df-based N derivation performed.

Candidate Ns are worker-year observations, not unique workers, countries, firms or clusters. Section 4 (printed p. 11) defines domestic incumbent workers in establishments/firms with hires from both MNE and domestic firms, retained as a balanced panel. Table A2 Ns are model-specific and differ from the baseline counts stated in that prose for Ireland; use the table values as candidates only. Exact attribution of any candidate N to an assigned row remains unresolved.

Reported success is scoped to the baseline multinational-spillover analysis identified by Table A2 / Table-Figure 5, for which authors explicitly describe spillovers across all specifications. It is not a claim of overall success for the paper: the abstract and introduction state that heterogeneity findings are not generally confirmed. This narrative field does not resolve panel/specification correspondence for the numeric fields.
